description: Expected outcomes for every fixture in fixtures/. The runner compares observed behavior against THESE assertions only; fixtures carry inputs, expected-results carries the assertions. kind=positive PASS means the security property held; kind=negative BOUNDARY-HELD means the gate behaved exactly as the documented claim ceiling says (it does not do things it never claimed). v2 extends the v1 set (C1–C3, N1–N4, unchanged) with consent/descriptor fail-closed cases (D*), scheduler-mode cases (S*), a legal-negative case (L1), eviction-boundary probes (E1/E2), and a nested-identity case (C4).

caseSet.note: Stable identifier for this exact fixture set. Any change to fixtures/ or to these expectations is a new case set and a new content version of the pack.

C2.claim: labeled read → later deny-sink call → denied automatically (label rule, plus identity rule on the verbatim reuse)

C3.claim: labeled result transformed inside a labeled tool → renamed forward → still denied via provenance/identity

C4.claim: labeled secret forwarded verbatim inside a nested sink argument → denied (identity rule's arg walk reaches nested leaves; label rule via whole-run threading)

D1.claim: unknown descriptor → fail-closed deny (rule descriptor-unavailable), zero executions, run still terminates normally

D2.claim: gateway ask_user escalation with no approval facility → fail-closed deny (rule consent-unavailable), zero executions

D3a.claim: same escalation with checkpointer wired → operator approval via the supported API executes the call once

D3b.claim: same escalation rejected → zero executions, human-review denial error, run ends without a final answer

L1.claim: legal negative: in a tainted run, benign non-sink tools still execute; only the declared deny-sink is blocked (strict sink refusal is the documented contract, not a false positive)

S1.claim: DAG scheduler (default, pinned): a sink submitted in a step AFTER the labeled read completed is denied (label + identity)

S2.claim: parallel scheduler: the same later-step script is denied identically — whole-run threading is scheduler-independent; batch-internal concurrency carries no happens-before guarantee and none is asserted

S3.claim: same-batch $ref dataflow ceiling: no provenance rule fires (the batch's gate evaluation precedes the read's observation), and the $ref substitution passes the read's raw result object which the string sink schema rejects — the sink never executes (fail-safe by typing, not by taint policy)

E1.claim: ledger capacity (default 512): all-sensitive overflow evicts the OLDEST observation — identity tracking degrades for the evicted secret while label containment persists on every check

E2.claim: eviction preference: the first NON-SENSITIVE (non-sensitive declared label) observation is evicted before any sensitive one — the oldest secret keeps identity tracking; label containment persists

N1.claim: unwired agent → provenance gate does not auto-fire

N2.claim: no resultTaintLabels profile → runtime does not invent secret labels

N3.claim: cross-run reuse → previous run's ledger does not survive

N4.claim: model-side transform of an in-context secret → the IDENTITY rule does not fire (that detection is NOT_ESTABLISHED); the call is still blocked by the label rule because whole-run threading denies every later deny-sink call in the run
